questions.q: Ethyl acetoacetate, CH₃COCH₂COOC₂H₅, is reduced with NaBH₄ in ethanol. The product is:
questions.explain: NaBH₄ reduces only the ketone to a 2° alcohol and leaves the ester intact. LiAlH₄ would reduce both groups and give butane-1,3-diol.

questions.q: Cinnamaldehyde, C₆H₅CH=CHCHO, is reduced with NaBH₄. In exam answers the product is taken to be:
questions.explain: NaBH₄ reduces the C=O and keeps the C=C. Excess LiAlH₄ is taken to reduce the C=C as well and give 3-phenylpropan-1-ol.

questions.q: Which compound is NOT reduced by NaBH₄ under normal conditions?
questions.explain: Amides and carboxylic acids do not react with NaBH₄. Aldehydes, ketones and acid chlorides are all reduced to alcohols.

questions.q: Why is NaBH₄ a much weaker reducing agent than LiAlH₄?
options: NaBH₄ has fewer hydrogen atoms per formula unit
Na⁺ is a stronger Lewis acid than Li⁺
Boron is more electronegative than aluminium, so the B–H bond is less polar
NaBH₄ is used in protic solvents, which destroy most of the hydride
questions.explain: The less polar B–H bond holds its hydride more tightly, so only reactive carbonyl groups are attacked. Both reagents have four hydrides, and NaBH₄ reacts only slowly with methanol, ethanol or water.
